question: How has phosphorus pollution in Lake Veyra changed since 2019, what drives it, and what is being done?

required_facts.fact: North basin mean TP was 38 µg/L in 2019
North basin mean TP fell to 29 µg/L in 2022
North basin mean TP was 26 µg/L in 2024
South basin TP stayed roughly stable (21 to 20 µg/L)
Algal bloom days fell from 41 (2019) to 22 (2024)
2021 study: Tamsin Creek ~55% of external load
2023 consultant review: Tamsin Creek ~30%, 2021 estimate too high; internal loading from sediments
Buffer strips on 12 farms by end of 2021
Two-year north basin aeration pilot starting summer 2025
Target: north basin TP below 25 µg/L by 2027
2022 was a dry year; part of the decline may reflect lower runoff

contradiction.description: Tamsin Creek share of external phosphorus load: 55% (2021 Council study, one wet year) vs ~30% (2023 consultant, three years + sediment cores)
contradiction.expectation: The report should present both estimates and explain the disagreement, not silently pick one.

nice_to_have: Budget cut 15% in 2024 and septic cost-share paused (2023_budget_memo.txt)
Volunteer sampling corps collected 61% of 2024 samples (2024_monitoring_update.md)
Late-summer TP spikes at deep stations with low oxygen in 2024, consistent with internal loading
